observedPatterns: Repeated nonblocking counterthreat replies make local-only opponent interpretations unreliable.
An immediate defense may route into a remote win or expanded parent-level choice.
Locally identical blocks in different children can produce different forced destinations.
Threats remain dormant across many intervening moves and must be rechecked after new marks.
A leaf gain can also create a parent threat; ownership trades are not equal merely because each side wins one leaf.
events.humanPerspective: These are interface demands observed during agent play. Human memory burden and attention-switch costs are research-informed hypotheses, not measured human gaze or thinking times.
brainstorm: Compare candidate move destinations in a small persistent preview while retaining the current board.
Show closed-target expansion explicitly, including which parent becomes legal.
Use scale-aware summaries for ownership, occupancy, and immediate threats rather than hiding all marks at overview.
Offer user-controlled bookmarks and back/forward camera history for repeated region visits.
Separate a selected candidate route from the last actual move route so hypothetical and observed chains are distinguishable.
Allow a chosen region to remain visible while navigating elsewhere; test pinned detail or a second view.
